module.title: TALOS fixed-contact whole-body inverse dynamics
entrypoints: exercizes/ex_3_biped_balance_with_gui.py (scientific setup reference; GUI not executed)
module.expensive_path: Repeated assembly and active-set solution of the floating-base acceleration/contact-force HQP, including rigid-contact Jacobians and inverse-dynamics constraints. Cost and acceleration value remain unmeasured until the Linux native probe; no speedup or benchmark timing is claimed.
module.rationale: One controller module maps a floating-base state and task references to acceleration, actuator torques and two rigid-foot contact-force distributions. CoM, hand/torso SE3 and posture objectives share the same hard dynamics/contact/actuation feasibility problem, so they are one module rather than separate robot or scenario modules.
excluded: Walking, contact transitions, external disturbances and measured external forces
Other robot embodiments and standalone manipulator/quadruped task families
Alternative solver backend comparison, MPC, RL and GPU implementation
GUI, forward torque simulator, collisions, objects and grasp contacts
hazards: PROVISIONAL: no native build or short test has run; Linux SSH connection is pending.
The curator directed proceeding on GitHub after the scope and source draft were presented; native evidence remains pending and PR #524 stays Draft.
Root BSD-2-Clause license coexists with historical LGPL notices; TALOS data has its own LGPL-3.0 notice.
The upstream model-path join needs a scratch adapter; source payload must remain unchanged.
Upstream scales effort limits by 1.45 and disables the velocity-bounds task; final scenario semantics need evidence.
Exact HQP output is non-unique; physical feasibility and task behavior must be checked without imposing optimizer identity.
The benchmark's NumPy-only verifier contract requires an explicit independent dynamics/FK design.
Right-hand and torso additions are proposed adaptations; official-test coverage and any custom-check status remain to be determined.
